Royal Palaces and Tombs Center (Korea Heritage Service) English page: Gyeongbokgung Palace and Its History, introduction
quotes: Gyeongbokgung Palace is the primary palace of the Joseon dynasty that was established in 1395
The name "Gyeongbok" means that "the new dynasty shall have good fortunes and prosper."
real_place.text: 경복궁은 1395년에 세운 조선 왕조의 법궁(으뜸 궁궐)이다. '경복'은 새 왕조가 큰 복을 누리며 번영하라는 뜻이다.
real_place.license: Korea Heritage Service official page; short factual paraphrase only

real_place.source_locator: Stories of Gyeongbokgung Palace > Gwanghwamun Gate (story id 20231123030313000617)
quotes: Gwanghwamun Gate is the main gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace.
Its name "Gwanghwa" means "virtuous influence by the King," and "-mun" is a suffix that denotes "gate."
Unlike other palaces' main gates, Gwanghwamun Gate has a double-roofed pavilion over a high stone foundation the way the gates of fortresses are built, boasting a magnificent aura.
The gate consists of three arched openings. The king used the central arch, while the crown prince and officials entered through the openings on either side.
The gate restored to its original shape and place as a wooden structure in 2010.
real_place.text: 광화문은 경복궁의 정문이다. '광화'는 '임금의 덕이 널리 비친다'는 뜻이다. 다른 궁궐 정문과 달리 높은 석축 위에 2층 누각을 올려 성문처럼 웅장하다. 홍예문 셋 중 가운데는 왕, 양옆은 왕세자와 신하가 썼다. 2010년 원래 모습과 자리에 목조로 복원되었다.
real_place.license: Korea Heritage Service official page; short factual paraphrase only

real_place.source_locator: Stories of Gyeongbokgung Palace > Geunjeongjeon Hall and Geunjeongmun Gate & Corridors (story id 20231123030313006700)
quotes: Geunjeongjeon Hall is the throne hall of the palace, where the king held a coronation ceremony, granted audiences to his officials, met foreign envoys and presided over large official functions.
"Geunjeong" means "to work diligently and perform a wise ruling,"
The hall is the largest and most formal hall in Gyeongbokgung Palace.
The courtyard also has stone posts that dictate state officials' positions by their ranks.
Behind the throne is a wall screen painted with the sun, moon and a five-peak mountain which symbolize royal authority.
Jeongjong, Sejong, Sejo, Jungjong and Seonjo were crowned king at Geunjeongjeon Hall
real_place.text: 근정전은 경복궁의 정전으로 즉위식, 신하 조회, 외국 사신 접견, 큰 국가 행사가 열렸다. '근정'은 '부지런히 일해 바르게 다스린다'는 뜻이다. 경복궁에서 가장 크고 격식 높은 건물이다. 앞마당에 품계석이 있다. 어좌 뒤 일월오봉도는 왕의 권위를 상징한다.
real_place.license: Korea Heritage Service official page; short factual paraphrase only

coordinates.basis: Wikipedia infobox (KHS page has no coordinates)

real_place.caveat: Coronation list differs from the Wikipedia extract (KHS: Jeongjong, Sejong, Sejo, Jungjong, Seonjo at the hall; Danjong, Seongjong, Myeongjong at the gate). Do not use the list in cards.

real_place.source_locator: Stories of Gyeongbokgung Palace > Gyeonghoeru Pavilion (story id 20231123030313005682)
quotes: "Gyeonghoe" means "a joyous banquet," and "-ru" is a suffix that denotes "pavilion."
It is built inside the pond in the western part of the palace's living quarters.
It served as a venue for large-scale feasts for the king, court officials, and foreign envoys.
Gyeonghoeru Pavilion was restored when Gyeongbokgung Palace was rebuilt in 1867
The pavilion's first floor consists of 48 high stone pillars: 24 round pillars and 24 square pillars.
On the hip rafter lies 11 decorative tiles in zodiac animal sign shapes, which is the most among Korea's buildings.
real_place.text: '경회'는 '즐거운 잔치'라는 뜻이다. 경회루는 궁궐 생활 공간 서쪽 연못 안에 지었고 왕·신하·외국 사신을 위한 큰 잔치를 열었다. 1867년 경복궁 중건 때 복원되었다. 1층은 높은 돌기둥 48개(원형 24, 사각 24). 지붕 마루의 잡상 11개는 국내 건물 중 가장 많다.
real_place.license: Korea Heritage Service official page; short factual paraphrase only
